To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the New Classical approach is not a useful guide to the interpretation of economic data and that the New Classical model does not provide a good representation of the real world.
the epistemology of economics is a mess and that the messiness is a function of the fact that the epistemological issues are not separable from the substantive issues.
the New Keynesians are right and the New Classical economists wrong.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the relationship between epistemology and economics, and we are particularly interested in the implications of the post-Modernist critique for the practice of economics.
the nature of economic knowledge and the ways in which it is acquired, and the nature and scope of its applications.
the development and application of economic theory and econometric techniques to problems in economics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no conclusive statements, and the editors of The Palgrave are to be congratulated for not seeking such a statement.

the epistemology of economics, as of any other discipline, is not a matter to be resolved but a matter to be lived with, and that the best that can be hoped for is that the epistemological limits are recognized, and the limitations of epistemology itself acknowledged.
there is no conclusive statement to be made.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the world is too complex to allow for a single, all-encompassing theory, and yet it is too simple to allow for a multiplicity of equally valid theories.

the epistemology of economics is a series of statements that have been made, some of which have been shown to be true or useful, some of which are not true or not useful, and some of which are neither true nor useful.

we have not yet been able to provide a satisfactory account of the conditions under which we can have confidence in our knowledge claims, and we are still a long way from being able to provide an account of the conditions of knowledge that would allow us to say that our knowledge claims are true or false (p. 2).
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no epistemological credentials, only the best we can do with our limited resources.

the epistemological status of economic knowledge, as with the substantive content, depends on the particular case, and that there are no general rules that will allow one to determine in advance whether or how any particular case can be resolved.
there are no epistemological guarantees of the truth of our statements, whether they be substantive economic ones or epistemological ones.
